title: Attributing Agent Failures to Their History Needs an Executed Counterfactual: Toward a Reporting Standard
abstract: arXiv:2611.05650v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Published explanations of why long-horizon agents fail are commonly taxonomies labeled over completed trajectories: a judge reads a transcript and names the failure. We argue that a claim attributing an agent's behavior to its history should carry intervention-verified evidence, per instance or via a validated estimator: freeze an executable mid-trajectory state, alter only the history the agent sees, and continue - executed rather than inferred from the transcript, at a state whose restoration has been measured, with a replay certificate matched to the estimand. Each of the four manipulation classes we name has a precedent, and several methods already execute interventions from checkpoints, re-executed prefixes or recorded conversation states (for example DoVer, REFLECT, Min et al., Who&When Pro, Causal Agent Replay), but none reports a measured replay certificate. translated_title: 将智能体失败归因于其历史需要执行的反事实验证：迈向一种报告标准
translated_abstract: 已发表的关于长程智能体为何失败的解释，通常是基于完整轨迹标注的分类法：由裁判阅读对话记录并命名失败类型。我们认为，将智能体行为归因于其历史的论断应当携带经干预验证的证据——无论是逐实例验证还是通过经验证的估计器：冻结一个可执行的轨迹中间状态，仅改变智能体所见的历史，然后继续执行——必须实际执行而非从对话记录中推断，且在恢复精度已被测量的状态下进行，并附带与估计目标相匹配的重放证书。我们所命名的四类操纵中每一类都有先例，且已有若干方法能从检查点、重新执行的前缀或记录的对话状态出发执行干预（例如 DoVer、REFLECT、Min 等人、Who&When Pro、Causal Agent Replay），但没有任何一项报告了经过测量的重放证书。随后我们给出两项警示性测量，均未应用该标准……
tldr: 该论文提出，将智能体失败归因于其历史的论断必须由实际执行的反事实干预来验证——冻结可执行的轨迹中间状态、仅改变历史并继续运行，同时报告经过测量的重放证书——并将其确立为一种新的报告标准。
en_tdlr: This paper argues that claims attributing agent failures to their history must be backed by executed counterfactual interventions—freezing an executable mid-trajectory state, altering only the history, and continuing—with measured replay certificates, proposing this as a new reporting standard.
